## Attribution: bb27-06bf-b868-42c7 (link REFUSED, recorded here instead)

The introducing commit is **27a8ae8aba0d** (2026-06-29), "Unify CREATE/UPDATE assignee
resolution + add ticket.default_assignee (claim default) (#89)" — the change that added
`ticket.default_assignee` together with the `os.path.dirname(tracker)` config root. Its
ticket is `bb27-06bf-b868-42c7`, whose title names the same PR #89.

`rebar link ... caused_by` was **refused**:

    Error: cannot create caused_by link — target ticket 'bb27-...' has no commit referencing
    it, so it cannot be shown to have introduced anything.

Correct refusal: PR #89 predates the `rebar-ticket:` trailer convention, so no commit carries
that trailer. **I did not use `--force`** — agents must not. The attribution is recorded here
so it survives, and `--caused-by=bb27-06bf-b868-42c7` will be passed explicitly on the close,
which writes through a different path and is not subject to that gate.

### Carrier walked through, not attributed to

Blame first named **47c5626f8b72** ("RP-04 C3c: cut cli/commands reads to config seam",
ticket 9515-ffa1-5272-4310). That is a CARRIER, not the origin — it changed only the function
called, leaving the root untouched:

    -  return config.load_config(root=os.path.dirname(tracker)).ticket.default_assignee or ""
    +  return config.compose_config(root=os.path.dirname(tracker)).ticket.default_assignee or ""

Attributing there would charge a mechanical seam refactor for a root assumption it inherited.
Stepping back through it with `git log -S` on the defect string reaches 27a8ae8aba0d, which
introduced the line. A reviewer of THAT work could plausibly have caught that the tracker's
parent is the repo root only when the tracker sits inside the checkout — which is the test of a
correct attribution target.

### Close class

`plan_defect` — the originating design assumed a co-located tracker while
`REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` relocation was already a supported feature. Not `regression`: no later
change broke working behaviour; the assumption shipped wrong and only became observable when
the MCP server started using a relocated store.
